Woke up coffee machine broke, went to buy a new one and my van broke. Took my frustratons out on this rusty old axe all afternoon. [Axe project update Day 1.]

Had an unplanned day off work due to lack of wheels. I blew my front wheel bearing out. Ended up borrowing my parents old truck a beat up F-250 Bush truck, with a short somewhere, if I shut it off for more then 20 minutes the battery dies and I have to boost it. Pretty annoying.

Axe is looking nice though, all I did was take it out of the vinegar bath, and sand off the rest of the rust, now I'm working on bringing the edge back with a Coarse file and a Bastard file. hopefully by tomorrow I'll be honeing the blade to razor sharp.

Honestly it cleaned up very nice, most of the rust was relatively loose on the surface. I think because it was on a wet mossy rock leaning against a tree that it acted as a natural anode/cathode type of thing and mostly just built up surface rust I'd describe the rust like a "loose fuzzy rust" Makes me think the axe might have been left out there for even less time,

It's still 100% solid, there are a couple spots on the top layer at the curves where a few fibres are startinbg to fray but 2 seconds with sandpaper will fix that, I'm going to do the handle after the head, I'm still debating what I want to do with it as far as finish goes. But it's still solid, no rot or chipping or even breakage inside the headstock at the connection, I am going to fill the headstock cavity gaps with epoxy though really just to stop moisture from getting inside. I'm debating sanding the entire handle to new wood and then oiling or staining it, or just leaving it how it is. I'm definitely drilling a lanyard/hanger hole in it though. Maybe even plasti-dip it for grip.
